overview: Fox Corporation is a U.S. media company built around live news and sports programming, operating the FOX broadcast network, Fox News Media, Fox Sports, Fox Entertainment, and the free ad-supported streaming service Tubi. The company's strategy centers on monetizing live, appointment-viewing content (NFL, college football, MLB postseason, breaking news) across linear, affiliate, and direct-to-consumer channels, most recently via its new FOX One streaming app. Fox operates almost entirely in the U.S. market and, following its June 2026 agreement to acquire Roku for roughly $22 billion, is pursuing a transformation from a pure content company into a combined content-and-distribution platform.

business_model.summary: Fox generates revenue from three interlocking streams: affiliate/subscription fees paid by pay-TV distributors and vMVPDs for carriage of its cable networks (Fox News, FS1, Big Ten Network) and broadcast retransmission consent; advertising sold across linear broadcast/cable, digital, and Tubi; and a fast-growing direct-to-consumer subscription stream from FOX One (launched August 2025, $19.99/month or $199.99/year). Live sports rights (NFL, MLB, Big Ten, WWE) and Fox News' ratings dominance are the anchor assets that pull both affiliate fees and advertising. Revenue is a mix of highly recurring (multi-year affiliate contracts, growing DTC subscriptions) and cyclical/event-driven (advertising spikes in Olympic/World Cup and election years, NFL season skew toward Q2/Q3 fiscal quarters).

revenue_streams.name: Affiliate fees (cable/retrans)
revenue_streams.trend: stable to slightly growing (rate increases offset subscriber losses)

revenue_streams.name: Advertising (linear + digital + Tubi)
revenue_streams.trend: growing, event-driven (FY2026 boosted by FIFA World Cup)

revenue_streams.name: Other / DTC subscription (FOX One, licensing)
revenue_streams.trend: growing rapidly off a small base

business_model.customer_type: B2B (pay-TV/vMVPD distributors, advertisers/agencies) and increasingly B2C (Tubi viewers, FOX One subscribers)
business_model.geographic_mix: Overwhelmingly United States; minimal direct international revenue exposure versus global media peers

main_competitors: Paramount Skydance (CBS, forthcoming Warner Bros. Discovery combination)
competitive_position.market_position: Fox News is the #1-rated cable news network by a wide margin; FOX broadcast network holds top-tier NFL and college football rights; Tubi is the largest free ad-supported streaming (FAST) service in the U.S. by engagement, ahead of Roku Channel and Pluto TV

moat_factors.factor: Live sports and news content scarcity
moat_factors.description: Long-term NFL, MLB, Big Ten and college football rights plus Fox News' loyal, highly engaged audience create appointment viewing that is difficult to replicate and resistant to DVR/streaming time-shifting, sustaining ad and affiliate leverage
Decades of dominant ratings among conservative-leaning viewers provide a durable, high-margin cable asset even as the broader cable bundle shrinks

100M+ monthly active users, ~13.2B hours viewed in FY2026 (+20% YoY), revenue growth over 25% in FY2026 gives Fox a leading position in ad-supported streaming, though Roku Channel, Pluto TV (WBD/Paramount) and Amazon Freevee are strong rivals

moat_factors.factor: Lean cost structure / no legacy studio or theme park drag
moat_factors.description: Fox spun off entertainment/film assets to Disney in 2019, leaving a focused, high-margin news/sports/broadcasting portfolio with fewer content write-off risks than integrated studio peers

If completed, direct ownership of a leading CTV operating system and 100M+ device relationships would convert Fox from a content licensor dependent on third-party platforms into an owned-and-operated distribution platform with first-party data and ad tech

weaknesses: Small scale versus Disney, Comcast, Netflix, and a combined Paramount-WBD in overall content library and streaming subscriber base
No major scripted entertainment or film studio (spun off to Disney in 2019), limiting content breadth versus larger peers
Structural cord-cutting continues to erode the traditional affiliate-fee base that still funds roughly 40% of revenue
Heavy reliance on a small number of marquee sports contracts (NFL in particular) whose costs escalate faster than revenue in each renewal cycle
Dual-class share structure concentrates voting control with the Murdoch family (via Lachlan Murdoch), limiting minority shareholder influence over major strategic decisions including the Roku deal

growth_drivers: FOX One direct-to-consumer streaming app, launched August 2025, exceeded subscriber expectations in its first year and extends monetization to cord-cutters/cord-nevers without cannibalizing affiliate revenue
Tubi's continued audience and revenue growth (FY2026 revenue up >25% YoY, viewing hours up 20% YoY) as advertisers shift budget to ad-supported streaming

Pending ~$22B acquisition of Roku (announced June 2026), which would combine Fox's content with Roku's CTV operating system, The Roku Channel, and first-party data reaching 100M+ streaming households — expected to be FCF-per-share accretive by year two post-close with ~$400M of run-rate cost synergies
Marquee live sports calendar (NFL, Big Ten/college football, MLB postseason, WWE) continuing to command premium advertising CPMs and anchor retransmission negotiations

Event-driven advertising tailwinds: FY2026 benefited materially from FIFA World Cup coverage (Q4 advertising revenue +78% YoY); future World Cup/Olympics-adjacent cycles and election-year political advertising provide periodic upside
Continued affiliate rate increases per subscriber even as the subscriber base shrinks, partially offsetting cord-cutting
Large ongoing capital return program (dividend increases, $12B cumulative buyback authorization, ~36% of shares repurchased since the 2019 spin) supporting per-share metrics

business.description: Continued pay-TV subscriber losses pressure the affiliate-fee revenue base that funds roughly 40% of company revenue

NFL and other live-sports rights costs are rising industry-wide (total U.S. sports-rights spend near $36.5B in 2026, up ~75% since 2021); Fox must absorb higher rights fees at the next renewal without proportionate revenue growth

business.risk: Concentration in Fox News and NFL
business.description: A large share of profitability depends on the continued ratings dominance of Fox News and the value of NFL programming; any erosion in either would disproportionately affect results
Successfully integrating a large, previously independent ad-tech/CTV platform (Roku) carries typical M&A execution risk around technology, culture, and realizing the targeted $400M in synergies

financial.description: The Roku transaction (~$22B enterprise value, cash-and-stock) will require Fox to fund a substantial cash component ($96/share cash plus stock), potentially increasing leverage or requiring new debt issuance
Fox faces termination fees of approximately $866M (general) or $1.2B (regulatory-failure specific) if the Roku deal collapses
Management has guided the Roku deal to be FCF-per-share accretive only by the second full year after closing, implying near-term dilution or integration costs

regulatory.risk: DOJ antitrust review of Roku deal
regulatory.description: The Department of Justice has widened its review and issued a 'second request' for additional information, examining whether Fox could favor Tubi/Fox content within the combined Roku platform and whether combining the two largest FAST services (Tubi and Roku Channel) under one owner reduces consumer choice; deal completion timeline and terms are at risk
Senators (e.g., Sen. Warren) have formally raised concerns to DOJ about the deal's platform-control implications, adding political visibility to the antitrust review
Early NFL rights renewal discussions with FOX and CBS have reportedly run into FCC-related obstacles, adding uncertainty to future sports-rights economics
Fox News has faced high-profile defamation litigation in the past (Dominion settlement); similar litigation risk remains a recurring feature of the news business

macro.description: Advertising revenue (~45% of total) is sensitive to macroeconomic conditions and marketing budget cuts in a slowdown; FY2026 was flattered by non-recurring FIFA World Cup ad spend that will not repeat in FY2027
Rising rates increase the cost of any new acquisition-related debt and pressure the equity multiple of a company reliant on capital returns
A crowded DTC streaming market (Netflix, Disney+, Max, Paramount+, Peacock, Amazon, plus FOX One) risks subscriber-acquisition cost inflation and churn as consumers rationalize spend

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. traditional pay-TV continues to decline structurally (~mid-to-high single digit percentage subscriber losses per year industry-wide) while streaming/FAST viewing and ad dollars grow; live sports and news remain the most resilient linear content categories and are driving continued consolidation (Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger cleared 2026; Fox-Roku pending) as scale and owned distribution become more important
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — advertising revenue is macro-sensitive and event-driven (World Cup, Olympics, election cycles create periodic spikes), while affiliate and subscription revenue is more resilient and contractual
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct exposure historically given net cash-light balance sheet and steady FCF, but rising given the pending debt-and-cash-funded Roku acquisition
key_input_costs: Sports programming rights (NFL, college football, MLB, Big Ten)
Technology/platform investment (Tubi, FOX One, prospective Roku integration)

recent_developments.event: Reported record Q4 and full-year FY2026 results: FY2026 revenue $17.13B (Q4 $4.21B, +28% YoY), FY2026 net income $1.73B, FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA $3.91B; Q4 advertising revenue surged 78% YoY on FIFA Men's World Cup coverage
Board authorized an additional $5B in stock buybacks, bringing cumulative repurchase authorization to $12B; increased semi-annual dividend to $0.29/share

Announced definitive agreement to acquire Roku, Inc. for approximately $22B enterprise value ($160.00/share via $96.00 cash + 0.9693 FOX Class A shares per Roku share); existing FOX shareholders would own ~73% of the combined company post-close

DOJ has widened antitrust review of the Roku deal, issuing a 'second request' for documents; concerns center on Fox potentially favoring Tubi/Fox content on the combined Roku platform and consolidation of the two largest FAST services (Tubi and Roku Channel); U.S. Senators have formally petitioned DOJ regarding the deal

FOX One direct-to-consumer streaming app launched ahead of the 2025 college football/NFL season at $19.99/month; exceeded internal subscriber expectations by fiscal year-end, with growth concentrated outside the traditional pay-TV bundle
Tubi delivered record results: revenue growth of more than 25% YoY, ~13.2B viewing hours (+20% YoY), 100M+ monthly active users, content library expanded to 350,000+ titles

Murdoch family resolved multi-year Nevada trust litigation; new family trust (expiring 2050) gives Lachlan Murdoch sole voting control over Fox Corporation and News Corp, while siblings James, Elisabeth and Prudence exited as trust beneficiaries in exchange for ~$3.3B in stock, removing a longstanding governance overhang

Sell-side maintained largely bullish stance post-Q4: Wells Fargo and Bank of America both reiterated Buy ratings with ~$70 price targets; consensus average target ~$70, with 52% of 48 analysts rating Buy/Strong Buy and no Sell ratings, though the stock has traded choppily on Roku-deal antitrust headlines

items.target: $0.29/share semi-annual (~$245M aggregate annual cash dividends based on FY2026 year-end share count)
items.notes: Increase announced alongside Q4 FY2026 results
Company has repurchased ~36% of shares outstanding since the 2019 spin-off, cumulative $10.7B of capital returned to date
Deal expected to be free-cash-flow-per-share accretive by the second full fiscal year after closing; close subject to DOJ second-request review, shareholder votes, and other customary conditions

items.target: No explicit numeric subscriber/revenue target disclosed
items.notes: Management characterized FOX One as having exceeded internal expectations and Tubi as continuing double-digit revenue growth momentum entering FY2027, without publishing a specific subscriber count or revenue figure

guidance.management_commentary: Management emphasized FY2026 as a record year (revenue and Adjusted EBITDA) underpinned by the FIFA World Cup advertising boost, the successful FOX One launch, and continued Tubi audience/revenue growth, while positioning the pending Roku acquisition as the next leg of a long-term digital and distribution strategy. Leadership reiterated confidence that FOX will retain flexibility on future affiliate and sports-rights negotiations and stressed continued heavy capital return to shareholders even while funding the Roku transaction.

bull_case: Live news (Fox News) and marquee live sports (NFL, college football, MLB) remain the most DVR/streaming-resistant content categories, sustaining affiliate and advertising leverage even as the broader pay-TV bundle shrinks
FOX One and Tubi give Fox two distinct, fast-growing direct-to-consumer/FAST revenue streams that convert cord-cutters into new monetizable relationships rather than pure cannibalization

The pending Roku acquisition, if it clears antitrust review, would transform Fox from a content licensor into an owned CTV distribution platform with 100M+ device relationships, first-party ad data, and ~$400M in targeted cost synergies — a structural re-rating catalyst

Disciplined, shareholder-friendly capital allocation: $12B cumulative buyback authorization (already retired ~36% of shares since 2019), rising dividend, and consistently strong free cash flow generation
Murdoch family governance overhang resolved (2025 trust settlement gives Lachlan Murdoch clear, uncontested voting control), removing a multi-year litigation/uncertainty risk for investors
bear_case: DOJ has escalated its antitrust review of the Roku deal with a second request; regulators and Senators have specifically flagged the risk of Fox favoring its own content (Tubi) on a combined platform and consolidating the two largest FAST services — the deal could be blocked, delayed, or restructured, and termination fees (~$866M-$1.2B) create real downside if it fails

Structural cord-cutting continues to erode the affiliate-fee base (~40% of revenue) with no sign of reversing, and sports-rights costs (NFL especially) are rising faster than industry-wide, squeezing margins at the next renewal cycle
FY2026's record results were significantly flattered by a non-recurring FIFA World Cup advertising boost (Q4 ad revenue +78% YoY); FY2027 faces a difficult comparison without an equivalent event
Even if completed, the Roku deal is guided to be FCF-per-share dilutive until the second full year post-close, and integrating a large ad-tech/CTV platform carries meaningful execution risk

Dual-class share structure concentrates control with the Murdoch family (Lachlan Murdoch), limiting public shareholders' influence over major capital allocation and M&A decisions such as the Roku transaction
